raw.description:
About PatientIQ

PatientIQ is a fast-growing health tech company on a mission to improve patient outcomes. We partner with healthcare providers, medical device companies, and researchers to collect, analyze, and act on patient-reported outcomes data at scale â powering smarter clinical decisions and accelerating the future of value-based care.

Headquartered in Chicago and backed by top-tier venture capital and major health system investors, PatientIQ is building the largest platform for healthcare providers, industry partners, and researchers to collaborate on what matters most: helping patients get better.

The opportunity

PatientIQ is hiring a Strategy & Operations Lead to help drive the company's highest-priority strategic initiatives and strengthen the operating foundation required for our next phase of growth.

Working directly with the Chief of Staff and executive leadership team, you'll help build and scale our Strategic Program Office (SPO) - a new function responsible for governing the company's portfolio of strategic initiatives while improving how we plan, communicate, and execute across the business.

This role is ideal for a highly analytical operator who thrives in ambiguity, brings structure to complex problems, and enjoys turning strategy into execution.

What You'll Do

  • Own PatientIQ's portfolio of strategic initiativesâgoverning the company's highest-priority work from prioritization through execution, ensuring every initiative has clear ownership, measurable outcomes, and executive visibility
  • Lead complex cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution, partnering across Product, Commercial, Customer Success, Engineering, Finance, and Operations to deliver measurable business results
  • Help build and scale PatientIQ's Strategic Program Office (SPO) by establishing the governance, operating cadence, portfolio management, and accountability mechanisms that enable the company to execute at scale
  • Partner with the Chief of Staff and executive leadership team on strategic planning, executive operating rhythms, organizational priorities, board and leadership communications, and other high-impact initiatives critical to the business
  • Develop executive-ready analyses, recommendations, and communications that translate complex information into clear decisions, align stakeholders, and enable faster, higher-quality execution
  • Define and measure business impact by establishing KPI frameworks, tracking strategic initiatives, surfacing risks early, and ensuring investments deliver measurable operational and commercial outcomes
  • Champion AI-enabled ways of working by standardizing AI-powered workflows, automating manual processes, and embedding AI into how teams plan, communicate, analyze, and executeâcreating meaningful leverage across the organization
  • Drive accountability across the organization by clarifying ownership, facilitating decision-making, removing execution roadblocks, and maintaining momentum on the company's most important priorities

What Success Looks Like

We believe clarity drives performance. Here's what the first 90 days look like in this role:

30 days - Build strong relationships with executive stakeholders and functional leaders. Develop a deep understanding of PatientIQ's business, product, customers, strategic priorities, and operating cadence. Begin identifying opportunities to improve execution, communication, and operational efficiency. Become proficient with the company's AI tools and workflows.

60 days - Independently own one or more executive operating cadences. Lead a cross-functional strategic initiative with minimal oversight. Deliver executive-ready analyses and communications that enable faster decision-making. Begin establishing the SPO framework

90 days - Be recognized as a trusted partner to the Chief of Staff and executive team. Fully support the company's strategic initiative portfolio and executive reporting cadence. Launch the foundational components of the Strategic Program Office. Deliver measurable improvements in execution through AI-enabled workflows and standardized operating processes.

Requirements

What you bring

Required

  • 2-4 years of experience in management consulting, investment banking, private equity, corporate strategy, or business operations at a high-growth SaaS or technology company
  • Exceptional analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to structure ambiguous questions, identify the most important issues, and develop clear, actionable recommendations
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing concise, executive-ready materials independently
  • Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives and drive accountability across teams without formal authority
  • Strong business judgmentâyou understand when to analyze further, when to make a recommendation, and when to push an organization toward a decision
  • Highly organized and detail-oriented, with the ability to manage multiple high-priority initiatives while maintaining a clear view of the broader business context
  • Comfort operating in a fast-moving environment where priorities evolve, information may be incomplete, and the path forward is not always defined
  • High ownership mindsetâyou do not wait for perfect direction and are comfortable building structure, defining the work, and driving it to completion
  • Strong aptitude for AI and modern productivity tools, with an interest in using technology to improve analysis, communication, and organizational efficiency
  • Exposure to go-to-market strategy, revenue operations, product strategy, healthcare technology, or B2B SaaS is a strong differentiator
  • Bachelor's degree required

Nice to have

  • Previous experience in a healthcare technology environment

Benefits

Why PatientIQ

  • Mission-driven work. We're solving a hard problem that matters â improving patient outcomes through better data. Every person here is working on something real
  • True idea meritocracy. Great ideas win, regardless of title. We encourage every team member to challenge the status quo
  • World-class team. You'll work alongside people who are at the top of their fields in health tech, enterprise software, and clinical science
  • Fast-growing. We're building the largest platform for healthcare providers and industry to collaborate â and we're just getting started
  • Great benefits. Top-notch health, dental, and vision. 401(k). Flexible PTO â we trust you to take the time you need. Professional development stipends
  • Real ownership. This is not a role where you maintain someone else's playbook. You'll build, shape strategy, and see your impact directly

title: Rippling
description: The verdict Rippling is one of the strongest products you can buy if you run HR, IT, and finance as connected systems, and the review data backs that up: 4.8 across more than 14,000 G2 reviews and 4.9 on Capterra. The onboarding automation that provisions payroll, benefits, IT access, and a device in one move is the standout, and it earns its keep. Go in clear-eyed about two things: the modular, quote-based pricing stacks faster than people expect, and the first-week learning curve is real. Key features One employee record that drives everything Hire someone once and the record propagates everywhere: payroll, benefits, device provisioning, app access, and offboarding all read from it, so a department change updates downstream automatically. Automated payroll and tax compliance Rippling calculates payroll taxes and files them with the correct federal, state, and local agencies, supports multi-entity and global payroll for employees and contractors, and stores electronic W-2s and 1099s. One-click onboarding and offboarding A single flow sends offer letters, enrolls payroll and benefits, ships a device, and grants app logins; offboarding runs it in reverse, revoking access and triggering device returns. Benefits administration with payroll sync Over 500 EDI and API carrier integrations, integrated HSA/FSA/commuter accounts with automatic payroll-deduction sync, COBRA and ACA automation, and bring-your-own-broker support alongside Rippling's PEO and brokerage. 600+ out-of-the-box integrations Connects QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Guideline for 401(k), Checkr for background checks, plus identity and productivity tools, with real user provisioning, attribute mapping, and cross-app workflow automation. Modular HR, IT, and Finance products Buy the core Rippling Platform, then add only the products you need across HR (Payroll, Benefits, Learning, Performance), IT (Identity, Device, Inventory), and Finance (Corporate Cards, Expenses, Bill Pay). What it is Rippling is an HR platform that doesnât stop at HR. The core is a single employee record: hire someone once, and that record drives payroll, benefits, device provisioning, app access, and offboarding. Where most HR software treats the employee database as a system of record, Rippling treats it as a trigger. Change a personâs department and Rippling updates it everywhere downstream. Onboard a new hire and it enrolls them in payroll, sets up their benefits, ships a laptop, and grants the right app logins from the same flow. The product is sold in modules. Thereâs a core, required Rippling Platform, and then you buy what you need on top of it: HR products (Payroll, Benefits, Learning, Performance, Recruiting, Time & Attendance), IT products (Identity & Access, Device, Inventory), and Finance products (Corporate Cards, Expenses, Bill Pay). The pitch, and itâs a real one, is that all three sit on the same data, so the IT and finance sides arenât bolted-on afterthoughts. Who itâs for This is built for the company that has outgrown a point HR tool but is also tired of running payroll in one place, device management in another, and expense reports in a third. If youâre hiring across multiple states or countries, Ripplingâs strongest. It runs multi-entity and global payroll, stores W-2s and 1099s, and handles contractors through dedicated products. Reviewers who pay people internationally describe currency conversion and cross-border pay as something Rippling âjust takes care of.â Itâs a worse fit for a simple operation. If you have fifteen domestic employees, one benefits plan, and no real IT footprint, the all-in-one model is overkill, and reviewers say exactly that, warning that simpler teams risk overbuying. Youâd be paying for breadth you wonât use and absorbing a configuration burden you donât need. Rippling rewards companies that genuinely run HR, IT, and finance as connected systems. If those live in separate departments that never talk, you lose the main reason to buy it. Why it stands out Onboarding and offboarding is the standout, and itâs not close. Capterra logs 97% positive mentions on onboarding, with reviewers describing clear step-by-step guidance to add employees, configure payroll, and connect benefits. business.com calls it a major strength. The thing people keep describing is âone-click onboardingâ that provisions payroll, IT access, and a device in a single action, and the same automation runs in reverse at offboarding, revoking access and triggering device returns. The January 2026 release added advanced Microsoft 365 offboarding actions, which is exactly the kind of detail that matters when someone leaves. The unified platform is the second genuine win. Capterra users rate the all-in-one dashboard 98% positive, and reviewers repeatedly call out Ripplingâs UI as the best theyâve used in an HRMS. Collapsing payroll, benefits, and people data into one synced record removes the manual re-entry and the reconciliation errors that plague stitched-together stacks. Integration breadth is the third. Rippling ships 600+ (the FAQ says 650+) out-of-the-box integrations: QuickBooks, Xero, NetSuite, Guideline for 401(k), Checkr for background checks, plus the usual identity and productivity tools, with real provisioning and attribute mapping, not just data export. Reviewers call this exceptional. The one caveat worth flagging: Expert Market notes Rippling doesnât natively integrate with third-party HR systems, so the strength is in app provisioning and internal cross-module sync rather than swapping out parts of the HR stack. Pricing in plain language Rippling starts around $8 per employee per month, but that number tells you very little. The real model is modular and quote-based: thereâs no full price list on the site, and some products carry a monthly base fee on top of the per-employee rate. You buy the core platform, then add each product separately. Thatâs the flexibility selling point and the budgeting headache in one. Hereâs where the wall is: the modules stack. Independent reviewers are consistent on this, the per-employee base is reasonable, but as you add Benefits, Device Management, Expenses, and the rest, the total climbs in ways that arenât obvious upfront. The most common complaint across G2, Capterra, and third-party reviews isnât that Rippling is bad value, itâs that the total cost is hard to see coming. Benefits administration is a particular gotcha: itâs a separate paid module, which is why business.com calls benefits a ânotable weaknessâ on cost grounds, though those fees can be waived if Rippling is your broker or PEO. Get a real quote before you fall in love with the demo, and price the modules youâll actually turn on, not the ones that look nice in the sales deck. Limitations The learning curve is real. The same feature density that makes Rippling powerful makes it overwhelming on day one. G2 reviewers describe it as a lot to absorb, especially for new admins. This is the cost of the all-in-one model, and itâs worth budgeting setup time for. Stability is the more concerning one. Capterra reviewers flag platform bugs and slow loads (48% negative) and auth or session timeouts (46% negative), and the mobile app comes up as occasionally buggy and missing features the desktop version has. More seriously, payroll, the thing you most need to be boring and correct, has edge cases. Capterra reviewers report incorrect overtime calculations that forced them to claw back overpayments, and Thrivea notes tax edge-case issues. The payroll engine is rated highly overall, with a 100% error-free filing guarantee cited by business.com, but the exceptions are the kind you remember. Reporting is the quieter gap. 43% of Capterra mentions on reporting are negative, centered on a lack of customization. If you need to slice your people data in non-standard ways, expect to fight the report builder. Benefits enrollment is the last one worth naming: Thrivea reports the workflows can feel clunky or incomplete, which is part of why benefits sentiment runs mixed even though the payroll-to-deduction sync is well liked. The bottom line If youâre a growing company running HR, IT, and finance as connected systems, especially across states or borders, Rippling is one of the strongest products you can buy, and the review data backs that up. The onboarding automation alone earns its keep, and the unified record genuinely removes work. Buy it for the integration, not just the HR. But go in clear-eyed. Get a real quote and add up every module youâll switch on, because the stacking is where people get surprised. Budget setup time for the learning curve. And if youâre a small, single-country team with simple benefits and no IT footprint, this is more platform than you need, youâll pay for breadth you wonât touch. Rippling rewards complexity. Bring it the right kind, and itâs excellent. What people are saying online Rippling is one of the most highly rated HR platforms I track, 4.8 across more than 14,000 G2 reviews and 4.9 on Capterra. Users love the unified dashboard and the way onboarding fires off payroll, benefits, and IT setup in one move. The platform is most positive for growing companies that genuinely run HR, IT, and finance together and have the bandwidth to configure it. The recurring frustrations are the same ones every time: a steep first-week learning curve, occasional bugs and slow loads, and a modular price tag that stacks up faster than people expect. Drawn from independent reviews and discussions, separate from our methodology score. What people love Onboarding logs 97% positive mentions, one click provisions payroll, benefits, IT access, and ships the device Capterra All-in-one platform rated 98% positive for collapsing payroll, benefits, and people data into one synced record Capterra Cited as the best HRMS UI reviewers have used, intuitive and genuinely modern Multiple Direct deposit (97%) and payroll entry (95%) rated highly; international pay 'just gets taken care of' G2 600+ third-party app integrations praised as exceptional for provisioning and cross-app automation Independent reviews Common complaints Sheer number of features overwhelms new users; admin configuration carries a real learning curve G2 Platform stability complaints, bugs and slow loads (48% negative) plus auth/session timeouts (46% negative) Capterra Reporting lacks customization (43% negative) Capterra Payroll edge cases bite, including incorrect overtime calculations that forced overpayment recovery Multiple Opaque, quote-based pricing with add-ons that 'stack' into surprise total cost Multiple Rippling alternatives #2 Gusto 3.9 #3 Deel 3.9 #4 TriNet 3.6 Where Rippling ranks HR Platforms #1 of 6 3.9 Best for ops-heavy and multi-country teams that want HR, IT, and finance running off one synced employee record. But go in clear-eyed. Get a real quote and add up every module youâll switch on, because the stacking is where people get surprised. Budget setup time for the learning curve. And if youâre a small, single-country team with simple benefits and no IT footprint, this is more platform than you need, youâll pay for breadth you wonât touch. Rippling rewards complexity. Bring it the right kind, and itâs excellent.

About Bizee

Bizee has helped nearly two million entrepreneurs start and run their businesses. Now we are building what comes next: an AI-powered Entrepreneur Operating System that helps founders launch, operate, stay compliant, and grow with less friction and more confidence.

We are profitable, founder-led, and operating at a clear inflection point. The next chapter requires a stronger operating system for how we hire, lead, communicate, develop talent, and scale execution across the company.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness to serve as a strategic partner to the President and executive team.

This is not a maintenance HR role. It is a builder-operator role for someone who can create clarity, raise the talent bar, strengthen the leadership layer, and build the people systems that help Bizee scale without unnecessary complexity or organizational drag.

As Bizee grows and transforms, one of the most important responsibilities of this role will be building and protecting a high talent bar. We are not simply adding headcount; we are intentionally increasing talent density across the company. This leader will help ensure we hire high-caliber builders, operators, and leaders who raise the standard, strengthen execution, and fit the culture we are building.

You will help design how Bizee hires, onboards, develops, manages, communicates, and performs as we move into our next stage of growth.

What You Will Own

  • Partner with the President and executive team on org design, leadership effectiveness, talent quality, succession, performance, and cross-functional friction
  • Design and protect Bizee's talent bar. Build the hiring standards, role scorecards, interview calibration, decision rules, and leadership alignment required to consistently identify high-caliber talent as the company scales. Ensure we do not compromise on quality-of-hire in the name of speed
  • Design a scalable hiring system, including workforce planning, role definition, scorecards, interview loops, calibration, decision frameworks, and candidate experience
  • Build Bizee's People Operating System, including the rhythms, mechanisms, and rituals that drive alignment, accountability, and performance
  • Strengthen the manager layer through practical enablement, feedback systems, performance routines, and leadership expectations
  • Design and own Bizee's performance cycle: goal setting, ratings, calibration, and linkage to comp and promotion decisions
  • Advise on role clarity, leveling, compensation philosophy, incentive design, spans, layers, and capability planning
  • Build onboarding, engagement, and internal communication mechanisms that help employees ramp faster and stay connected to the mission
  • Lead change management as Bizee modernizes its platform, operating model, AI-enabled workflows, and distributed teams
  • Plan and execute the eventual transition away from full co-employment (PEO) arrangements in multiple countries globally, including building the internal HRIS, payroll, benefits and compliance infrastructure needed to stand up direct employment, sequencing the migration to minimize risk and disruption, and managing the associated legal, tax, and employee communication considerations.
  • Own multi-state wage and hour compliance and workforce administration for a distributed employee population spanning nearly all 50 U.S. states, encompassing both exempt and non-exempt staff
  • Lead and integrate teams across multiple countries internationally, ensuring a single coherent Bizee culture and set of operating standards translate effectively across geographies, management structures, and local labor norms

Requirements

What You Will Bring

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in People, Talent, HRBP, Organizational Effectiveness, or People Operations leadership
  • Experience building People systems from the ground up, ideally in a high-growth, profitable, founder-led, PE-backed, SaaS, platform, marketplace, or tech-enabled services environment
  • Strong executive judgment and the ability to operate as a true strategic partner to a President and executive team
  • Proven experience with hiring systems, talent calibration, performance management, manager enablement, org design, leveling, compensation frameworks, and People Ops infrastructure
  • A strong point of view on talent density, quality-of-hire, leadership standards, and what it takes to build a high-performance company
  • Strong operator instincts: structured, practical, clear, and biased toward action
  • High EQ and high backbone: able to coach leaders, challenge assumptions, handle sensitive issues, and create clarity without adding drama or bureaucracy
  • Strategic and hands-on: able to advise the executive team in the morning and fix an onboarding workflow in the afternoon
  • Business-first orientation: understands revenue, margin, productivity, execution, and the tradeoffs of scaling a profitable company
  • Low-drama, high-signal communication style: brings facts, judgment, candor, and calm to complex situations
  • Culture carrier: protects what makes Bizee special while raising the performance bar
  • Comfort operating in ambiguity and building while the business is moving fast
  • Strong written communication skills and the ability to turn messy organizational issues into simple plans and operating mechanisms
  • Demonstrated experience managing a multi-state U.S. workforce (ideally 40+ states) that includes both exempt and non-exempt employees, with working knowledge of state-by-state wage and hour variation and how to operationalize compliance without adding unnecessary drag
  • Experience leading or partnering with teams in multiple countries, with a track record of integrating culture, standards, and management practices across borders rather than running parallel, disconnected functions
  • Direct experience transitioning a workforce out of a co-employment/PEO model, including standing up in-country or in-state direct employment infrastructure (payroll, benefits, statutory compliance) and managing the change process for affected employees and managers

What Success Looks Like

  • In the first year, Bizee has a stronger People Operating System that improves alignment, ownership, speed, and accountability across the company
  • Hiring is more structured, faster, and higher-signal. Leaders know what great looks like by role and level, hiring decisions are more disciplined, and the company is increasing talent density as it scales
  • Managers are better equipped to set direction, coach performance, handle conflict, and create clarity. Employees have stronger expectations, better communication, and a clearer understanding of how their work connects to the company's mission

The Head of People & Organizational Effectiveness becomes a trusted advisor to the President, executive team, and leadership layer, helping Bizee scale with discipline, clarity, high standards, and good judgment.

iPiD empowers financial institutions, payment service providers, and enterprises with a single global API for Know Your Payee (KYP) verificationâreducing fraud, reducing costs, staying compliant, and streamlining cross-border payments, globally.

We are a fast-growing fintech startup, founded by a global team of industry veterans from iconic organizations like SWIFT and Thomson Reuters. Supported by leading investors such as Monk's Hill Ventures, Jungle Ventures and Saison Capital, and guided by an advisory team featuring C-suite leaders from Microsoft, Commonwealth Bank, and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Our team combines global expertise with local insights; we are present across key citiesâincluding Singapore, Hanoi, Kuala Lumpur, Mumbai, Amsterdam, Brussels, Paris, London, New York, and Dubai.

Role Overview

As Sales Director you will play a key role in driving business growth by identifying and securing new opportunities across the region. This is a high-impact commercial role for someone who thrives on building strategic relationships, opening new markets, and delivering revenue growth within the cross-border payments industry. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will help shape our commercial strategy and expand our presence across Europe.

Core Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement commercial strategies according to company goals and objectives aiming to accelerate growth across Europe
  • Conduct market research and analysis to create detailed business plans on commercial opportunities (expansion, business development etc.)
  • Understand the requirements of existing customers to ensure their needs are being met
  • Act to acquire new customers and manage client relationships (new and existing)
  • Collaborate with and coordinate diverse teams (product management, marketing, customer success etc.)
  • Build and maintain profitable partnerships with key stakeholders
  • Monitor performance of commercial activities using key metrics and prepare reports for senior management
  • Assist in setting financial targets and budget development and monitoring

Requirements

  • Strong academic background in engineering, business, or comparable experience
  • Result-oriented with at least 5 years of experience and a track record in the payment industry, preferably cross-border payments
  • Proven experience as commercial director or other relevant role in the Europe
  • Proven experience in sales and/or marketing and managing relationships with key clients
  • In-depth understanding of market research methods and analysis
  • Solid knowledge of performance reporting and financial/budgeting processes
  • Commercial awareness partnered with a strategic mindset
  • Excellent organizational and leadership skills
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English and at least two major European languages (e.g., French, German, Spanish, or Italian).
  • Ability to communicate clearly and confidently with technical and business audiences
  • Candidates may be based anywhere in Europe and must have valid work authorization. Visa sponsorship is not available.

Benefits

What We Offer

  • Meaningful Impact - Play a key role in shaping the future of trusted cross-border payments and fraud prevention, helping solve critical challenges for financial institutions and businesses worldwide
  • Learn from experienced industry leaders - Join a team with deep expertise across payments, fintech and technology, and gain exposure to global customers and markets
  • Ownership & Growth - Join a fast-growing global fintech where your contributions are visible and valued, with the opportunity to participate in our Employee Stock Option Plan (ESOP) and share in our long-term success

_______________________________________________________________

Working in accordance with applicable laws, iPiD prohibits discrimination against any applicant or employee based on any legally-recognized basis, including, but not limited to: race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, childbirth or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, age, national origin or ancestry, citizenship status, physical or mental disability, genetic information (including testing and characteristics), veteran status, uniformed service member status or any other status protected by national or local laws of the jurisdiction in which the applicant resides.

If you need assistance or request accommodation during the recruitment process, please contact hr@ipid.tech

Please note that only shortlisted candidates will be notified. All information gathered will be treated in strict confidence and solely used for recruitment purposes.

____

To protect the interests of all parties, iPiD does not accept unsolicited resumes from a third party agency or search firm recruiters. Any unsolicited resumes sent to any iPiD employee, regardless of the means of transmission, will become the sole property of iPiD. We will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume.

description: Project Objectives: Support the IT Portfolio Governance function by ensuring projects are delivered on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with governance standards. The role is responsible for coordinating project governance activities, monitoring project costs and benefits, maintaining project documentation, and facilitating communication across project stakeholders. Key Responsibilities: Portfolio Governance Maintain project governance documentation and ensure project documentation checklists are up to date. Coordinate regular project meetings and prepare meeting materials. Organize monthly Portfolio Steering Committee (SteerCo) meetings. Monitor and review monthly project status across the portfolio. Coordinate with business users, Project Managers, and internal teams to ensure effective communication and alignment. Project Cost Management Monitor project cost trackers and ensure spending remains within the approved budget. Consolidate and prepare monthly project cost reports. Highlight cost variances and escalate potential risks when necessary. Project Benefit Tracking Maintain project benefit documentation and repository. Track, consolidate, and validate project benefit realization. Coordinate monthly benefit realization meetings with relevant stakeholders. Project Coordination & Governance Ensure project activities are executed according to the agreed timeline without unnecessary scope changes. Remind Team Leads of upcoming resource contract expirations to support workforce planning. Support the Portfolio Governance Lead with day-to-day governance activities. Perform additional ad hoc tasks based on business priorities. Required Skills Minimum 2 years of experience in IT Project Management, PMO, Project Governance, or IT Portfolio Management. Strong understanding of Software Development Life Cycle ( SDLC ), including Agile and Waterfall methodologies. Experience in project governance, PMO processes, project reporting, and portfolio management. Knowledge of project budgeting, cost tracking, and benefit realization. Understanding of project delivery, acceptance processes, and governance within a fast-paced environment. Excellent stakeholder management, coordination, and communication skills. Ability to prepare executive-level reports and presentation materials. Fluent in both English and Bahasa Indonesia, written and spoken. Portfolio Governance

title: Cashier
description: Job Summary Under general supervision, the Cashier performs clerical work in collecting payments from customers. Because the Authority has a responsibility to serve the public 24 hours a day, an employee in this class is expected to work overtime as conditions demand and on short notice during emergency conditions. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. Essential Duties & Responsibilities Receives cash payments from customers in partial and full payment of deposits, service fees, bills, invoices and other fees Uses cash register and keys in amounts paid; Because the Authority has a responsibility to serve the public 24 hours a day, an employee in this class is expected to work overtime as conditions demand and on short notice during emergency conditions.

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

  • Receives cash payments from customers in partial and full payment of deposits, service fees, bills, invoices and other fees
  • Uses cash register and keys in amounts paid; makes change as necessary
  • Receives and verifies check payments to ensure the correctness of the data, payee, payer, dollar amount, signature, and the amount written in words
  • Accepts mail payments and payments dropped in the overnight depository, and records amount paid on cash register
  • Clears cash register at the end of the day; totals stubs and receipts; counts cash and checks and compares total on cash register with currency in register to verify balances
  • Prepares deposit slips and daily cash summary showing monies collected
  • Accepts responsibility for shortages in cash collected
  • Performs other duties as assigned

Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

  • Thorough knowledge of regulations, practices, and procedures applicable to the collection and depositing of revenues
  • Ability to meet the character and reputation standards of a bonding company
  • Ability to keep records of cash received and to prepare a variety of routine reports on such transactions
  • Considerable knowledge of standard office practices and procedures
  • High degree of initiative and dependability
  • Some knowledge of the method and equipment used in data entry and computer utilization
  • Ability to plan work and carry through to completion without close supervision
  • Ability to use adding machines, copy machines and computer terminals
  • Ability to review documents to verify completeness and accuracy of information
  • Ability to deal effectively with all persons contacted during the course of work
  • Skill in counting money and recording transactions with speed and accuracy
  • Skill in the operation of adding machines and other mechanical office aids

Education & Experience

High School diploma, or equivalent, including or supplemented by courses in commercial subjects and four (4) years of progressively responsible experience in public contact work, three (3) years of which must have involved collecting and accounting for large sums of money.

  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Government Employees Retirement System (GERS)
  • Basic Life and AD&D Insurance
  • Voluntary Life Insurance
  • Long Term Disability Insurance
  • Supplemental Insurance
  • Personal Time Off (PTO)
  • 457b Deferred Compensation Plan
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

What Youâll Own

Customer-to-Product Translation

You will work with frontier AI labs, fast-growing AI startups, and enterprise AI teams to understand what they are trying to build, where their current stack breaks, and how Prime Intellect can become the infrastructure layer underneath their post-training and agent workflows.

You will turn vague, high-stakes customer conversations into clear technical and commercial strategy:

  • What is the customer actually trying to improve?

  • Is the wedge compute, evals, environments, sandboxes, managed RL, SFT, inference, or a full-stack workflow?

  • What should Applied Research build or prototype?

  • What needs to be packaged as product?

  • What should be in scope for a POC versus a long-term deployment?

  • What is the fastest path to a strong yes?

  • How do we explain Lab to different customer segments?

  • Which customer workflows should become reference architectures?

  • What should we productize versus deliver as managed work?

  • Where is the strongest wedge for enterprise customers?

  • Which signals show that a customer is ready for managed post-training?

  • A front-row seat to building the infrastructure layer for open AI
